title: Contract-driven fuzzing and runtime validation for KV cache eviction policies
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: We need a practical, reproducible validation system that proves correctness properties across the KV cache surface (LRU, TTL, and prefix-aware heuristics) while exercising interactions with continuous batching and GPU memory pressure. Current unit tests and fuzz harnesses exercise small kernels but miss multi-request interleavings, prefetch+evict races, and GPU fragmentation scenarios seen in production. This ticket builds a contract specification for eviction semantics, a fuzzing harness that emits replayable trace artifacts, and a lightweight runtime monitor to assert invariants in live canaries.
acceptance_criteria: A formal, human-readable contract.md that enumerates the expected semantics for LRU, TTL expiry, and prefix-aware eviction when requests are batched or prefetches are in-flight.
A fuzzing harness that generates >1000 unique eviction traces (including prefetch/eager-pin patterns) and produces replayable traces stored in S3/CI artifacts.
Runtime lightweight monitors integrated into the canary binary which detect and log violations of the contract at test/pilot scale without O(n) overhead.
A set of deterministic replay tests that reproduce at least two historical incidents from production traces or simulated GPU-fragmentation scenarios.
Green CI for the new fuzzing tests and monitors (passes in nightly pipeline) and at least one merged PR implementing monitor hooks and a fuzz target.
Performance regression <2% p50/p95 on canary workloads when monitors are enabled in sampling mode.
design_notes:
High level approach: 1) Define 'contract' as a set of predicates over trace events (pin, unpin, access, evict, ttl-expire, prefetch-start, prefetch-commit). Predicates include monotonic prefix consistency (if prefix A pinned then any dependent key should not be evicted until unpin), eviction observability (evicted keys must not appear in future cache hits for same prefix), and memory-safety (no double-free or use-after-free on GPU allocator).

The fuzz harness will produce interleavings of client requests, background prefetch tasks, explicit unpins, and simulated GPU OOM events. Each trace is serialized as a compact event log and fed to both the reference contract validator (user-space model implemented in Python/Go) and the runtime replay harness (native C++/Rust unit). We'll implement a 'contract verifier' library with two modes: static-assert (used by CI) and runtime-check (lightweight, sampling-based asserts emitting structured events to the console and log sink).

For GPU fragmentation scenarios, the harness includes a synthetic allocator that simulates slab fragmentation and returns allocation failures at tunable thresholds; eviction decisions should be provably sound even when allocation fails mid-batch. To avoid impacting production latency we will ship monitors with sampling and offload heavy analysis to an async worker that consumes trace artifacts.
implementation_plan: Write contract.md and review with runtime and SRE (owner: Marcus).
Create fuzz target 'kv_eviction_interleaver' in repo 'runtime/tests/fuzz' that emits replayable JSON traces (owner: Diego).
Implement reference validator in Python (tools/kv_contract_validator) for fast iteration and test vectors (owner: Sofia).
Add lightweight monitor hooks to canary build (sampling mode) that emit structured events to stdout/trace sink (owner: Marcus).
Add deterministic replay runner in CI that replays failing traces in debug mode and records heap/GPU allocator state (owner: QA).
Run extended fuzzing in CI-nightly for 72 hours and triage unique contract violations; produce a remediation backlog and link fixes to follow-ups.
test_plan: Property-based fuzzing: generate interleavings of 1-32 concurrent requests with variable sequence lengths, TTLs, and prefix sets.
Prefetch race scenarios: force prefetch commit after eviction decision and assert no stale hits occur.
GPU fragmentation simulation: tunable allocator with 5 fragmentation profiles that cause mid-batch allocation failures; assert no memory-safety violations.
Replay historical production traces anonymized and assert contract predicates hold; where they fail, generate minimum repro to file for debugging.
Integration test with continuous batching enabled: verify eviction decisions are stable when batching coalesces requests and when batch boundaries cross prefix boundaries.
Performance test: run canary with monitors enabled at 1% sample rate and measure latency regressions across p50/p95/p99.
Chaos test: inject transient allocator failures and ensure system falls back to compatible model variants without corrupting KV state.
